niveis.TEXTUAL: NIST links the concept/objective (Fig. 8, 3.1.1.x, glossary) AND both texts use equivalent terms verifiable on the cited pages; the LGPD-NIST correspondence itself is the agent's, neither source cites the other
niveis.INFERENCE: conceptual link made by the agent, without direct textual support; label it [inference]
niveis.NO_SUPPORT: LGPD topic with no equivalent in NIST IR 8062

lgpd_termos: propósitos legítimos, específicos, explícitos e informados
rows.nist: FIPP Purpose Specification and Use Limitation -> predictability (Fig. 8, p.26; text p.27; App. F p.49)
rows.justificativa: NIST links the FIPP to the predictability objective (p.27) and defines it as noticed purpose and compatible uses (p.49); the LGPD defines purpose as an informed purpose with no incompatible further processing (p.3). The LGPD-FIPP equivalence is the agent's comparison between the two texts.

rows.nist: Context (3.2.2.3) and predictability in the face of changes of context
rows.justificativa: Both use context as a criterion: the LGPD for compatibility with the informed purpose; NIST as a likelihood factor for a data action becoming a problem (p.31) and as a reason to assess changes of use (p.27).

rows.nist: FIPP Minimization -> manageability and disassociability (Fig. 8, p.26); disassociability 'most associated with minimization' (p.28)
rows.justificativa: Fig. 8 links Minimization to manageability and disassociability; p.28 says disassociability is the closest to minimization; the LGPD requires the minimum necessary and relevant, non-excessive data.

rows.lgpd: Art. 6º, IV (free access) and Art. 18, I-II
rows.nist: FIPP Access and Amendment -> manageability (Fig. 8, p.26; text p.27)
rows.justificativa: NIST lists access and amendment among the FIPPs enabled by manageability (p.27).

rows.nist: FIPP Quality and Integrity -> manageability (p.27); manageability makes it possible to correct inaccurate data
nist_termos: inaccurate information can be identified and corrected
rows.justificativa: p.27 says that without granularity inaccuracies cannot be corrected; App. F defines quality with accuracy, relevance, timeliness; the LGPD lists accuracy, relevance, updating.

rows.nist: FIPP Transparency -> predictability (Fig. 8, p.26; text p.26-27)
rows.justificativa: p.26 presents predictability as the basis of transparency and accountability; p.26 also suggests assessing whether the notice was read and understood, which complements Art. 9 (clear, adequate and conspicuous information).

rows.nist: FIPP Security -> confidentiality, integrity, availability (Fig. 8, p.26); App. F p.49
rows.justificativa: NIST aligns the Security FIPP with the CIA security objectives, not with the three privacy ones, and separates security from privacy (p.15-17).

rows.nist: Privacy problems: discrimination/stigmatization (Fig. 3, p.18; p.17)
rows.justificativa: Both address discrimination: NIST as a category of privacy problem; the LGPD as a principle.

rows.nist: FIPP Accountability -> predictability, manageability, disassociability (Fig. 8, p.26)
rows.justificativa: Accountability is the only FIPP aligned with all three objectives (Fig. 8). p.49: monitor, audit and document compliance; LGPD: demonstrate effective measures and their effectiveness.

rows.lgpd: Art. 18, III, IV and VI (correction, anonymization/blocking/deletion)
lgpd_termos: correção de dados incompletos, inexatos ou desatualizados
rows.nist: Manageability: granular administration including alteration, removal and selective disclosure (glossary p.36; Fig. 6 p.25)
rows.justificativa: The definition of manageability (alteration, removal) is the system capability that makes these rights feasible; NIST cautions that it is not a policy statement about the individual's right (p.27).

rows.nist: FIPP Individual Participation -> manageability (Fig. 8, p.26); App. F
rows.justificativa: App. F: seek the individual's consent to the extent practicable; manageability enables individual participation (p.27).

rows.lgpd: Art. 5º, XI (anonymization: loss of the possibility of association) and Art. 12
rows.nist: Disassociability: process PII without association to individuals beyond what is necessary (glossary p.36; p.28)
rows.justificativa: There is a textual echo of the association concept: the LGPD defines anonymization as the loss of the possibility of association to an individual; NIST defines disassociability as processing without association beyond the operational requirement.

rows.nist: Possible disassociability taxonomy: anonymity, de-identification, unlinkability, pseudonymity (p.28)
rows.justificativa: NIST lists pseudonymity among the terms of a possible taxonomy (p.28); the LGPD defines it in Art. 13 §4º. NIST does not detail techniques.

rows.lgpd: Art. 5º, XVII and Art. 38, sole paragraph (RIPD, data protection impact report)
rows.nist: PIA: analysis of how PII is handled, risks and ways to mitigate (p.23)
rows.justificativa: Both describe a document that analyzes processing, risks and mitigation. RIPD and PIA are not legal equivalents; the comparison is functional.

rows.lgpd: Art. 50 §1º and §2º, I, d (probability, severity; systematic assessment of impacts and risks)
lgpd_termos: probabilidade e a gravidade dos riscos
avaliação sistemática de impactos e riscos à privacidade
rows.nist: Risk model: risk = function of impact and likelihood (p.29-30)
rows.justificativa: The LGPD asks to consider probability and severity and to assess impacts and risks; NIST defines risk by likelihood and impact and introduces the problematic data action as a factor. The LGPD does not adopt the term 'problematic data action'.

lgpd_termos: desde a fase de concepção do produto ou do serviço
rows.nist: Privacy applied throughout the whole system life cycle (p.21)
rows.justificativa: Both require handling across the life cycle; the name 'privacy by design' is not in the LGPD and appears in NIST only as a reference to Cavoukian in note 2 (p.9).

rows.nist: Risk management: minimize adverse outcomes (p.21)
rows.justificativa: Conceptual connection (prevent harm / minimize adverse outcomes); neither text makes the link.

rows.lgpd: Art. 8º §5º and Art. 18, IX (revocation of consent)
rows.nist: Manageability (alteration and removal)
rows.justificativa: NIST does not mention revocation; the link is inferred from the definition of manageability.

rows.nist: Accountability: document compliance (p.49)
rows.justificativa: NIST asks to document compliance; the LGPD requires a record of operations without listing fields. Relationship inferred.

rows.lgpd: Art. 44 (security the data subject can expect)
lgpd_termos: segurança que o titular dele pode esperar
rows.nist: Predictability: do not surprise individuals with the processing (p.26)
rows.justificativa: Idea of legitimate expectation in both; link by inference.

rows.lgpd: Art. 10, II (legitimate expectations of the data subject)
rows.nist: Predictability and context (p.26-27, 31)
rows.justificativa: The data subject's expectations come close to 'reliable assumptions'; link by inference.

lgpd_termos: decisões tomadas unicamente com base em tratamento automatizado
rows.nist: Appendix E: big data and bias/discrimination in eligibility systems (p.47)
rows.justificativa: NIST describes the problem (bias in analytic systems) but proposes no right of review; thematic link.

rows.nist: PII security as the intersection of security and privacy (Fig. 2, p.16)
rows.justificativa: NIST does not address incident response (the term 'incident' is absent from the text); only the security/privacy intersection.

rows.nist: Senior Agency Official for Privacy (glossary p.36)
rows.justificativa: Privacy roles are not equivalent (the SAOP is accountable across the whole federal agency); merely analogous.

rows.nist: Evidence base to support trustworthiness claims (p.21, 24)
rows.justificativa: Both stress providing evidence; link by inference.

rows.nist: Context: email linked to a health condition (p.31)
rows.justificativa: NIST gives an example of sensitive context (health) without defining a special category; link by inference.

rows.lgpd: Art. 7º, caput and Art. 9º, III-IV (legal basis; identification of the controller)
lgpd_termos: somente poderá ser realizado nas seguintes hipóteses
rows.nist: FIPP Authority -> predictability (Fig. 8, p.26): have authority to process the PII and identify it in the notice (App. F p.49)
rows.justificativa: NIST asks to identify the authority (basis) in the notice; the LGPD requires a basis from Art. 7º and identification of the controller, but does not call this authority: relationship inferred.

rows.nist: (no equivalent)
rows.justificativa: NIST derives requirements from laws, regulations and FIPPs (Fig. 4, p.23) but has no list of legal bases.

rows.nist: (no equivalent; COPPA is cited only as an example of a law in note 47, p.22)
rows.justificativa: No treatment of children in NIST IR 8062.

rows.nist: (no equivalent)
rows.justificativa: NIST IR 8062 does not address international transfer.

rows.nist: (no equivalent)
rows.justificativa: No sanctions or data protection authority in NIST IR 8062 (the context is OMB A-130 and US federal agencies).

rows.nist: (no equivalent)
rows.justificativa: No civil liability regime in NIST IR 8062.

rows.nist: (partial: manageability mentions disposing of obsolete data, p.27)
rows.justificativa: There is no equivalent rule on end of processing; only the mention of disposing of obsolete data as a capability.

nist_sem_lgpd.conceito: Problematic data action as a risk factor
nist_sem_lgpd.obs: The LGPD does not use this concept; the RIPD (Art. 5º, XVII) speaks of processes that may generate risks to civil liberties and fundamental rights [inference by approximation].
The LGPD has anonymization/pseudonymization and necessity, but no equivalent system objective.

nist_sem_lgpd.conceito: Assessing effectiveness (notice read and understood) rather than the existence of the notice
nist_sem_lgpd.obs: The LGPD asks for clear and conspicuous information (Art. 9), without requiring a comprehension test.
